## Context & Motivation

::: {.callout-warning title="Key figures to remember"}
- **−69 %**: drop in the Living Planet Index (*Global Living Planet Index*) between 1970 and 2020
- **+1 °C**: rise in global temperatures above the 1951–1980 baseline
- Heat records: **2016** and **2020**
:::

**Central question**: Faced with crises (climate, biodiversity, inequality, governance), can finance help through **capital allocation**?

---

## Terminology — Synonyms

| French term | English term |
|---|---|
| Finance durable | Sustainable Finance |
| Investissement ESG | ESG Investing |
| Investissement socialement responsable (ISR) | Socially Responsible Investing (SRI) |
| Finance verte | Green Finance |
| Investissement responsable | Responsible Investment |
| Risque climatique | Climate Risk |
| Développement durable | Sustainable Development |

::: {.callout-note title="To remember"}
All these terms converge towards the same concept: integrating **non-financial** criteria into investment decisions.
:::

## The 3 ESG Pillars (MSCI 2023)

### Structure: 3 pillars → 10 themes → 37 key issues

| Pillar | Themes |
|---|---|
| **E — Environmental** | Climate change · Natural resources · Pollution & Waste · Environmental opportunities |
| **S — Social** | Human capital · Product responsibility · Stakeholder opposition · Social opportunities |
| **G — Governance** | Corporate governance ★★ · Corporate behaviour |

**★** = universal issue (all companies in the MSCI index)

**★★** = Board, Pay, Ownership, Accounting → directly contribute to the G score

### Selected key issues

**E**: Carbon emissions ★, Water Stress ★, Toxic Emissions ★, Clean Tech, Green Building

**S**: Labor Management ★, Health & Safety ★, Product Safety, Privacy & Data Security

**G**: Board ★★, Pay ★★, Business Ethics ★, Anti-Competitive Practices ★, Tax Transparency ★

---

## ESG Scoring

### Principles

- **Numerous systems**: MSCI, Sustainalytics, S&P Global, Refinitiv, Bloomberg, ISS ESG
- **Positive correlation** but **real divergence** between raters (*rating disagreement*)
- Example: R² ≈ **0.32** between Sustainalytics and MSCI (S&P 1200, Jan. 2016)

### MSCI Scale (since 2023)

$$\text{ESG Score} = \text{weighted average}(E,\ S,\ G)$$

| Rating | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **AAA / AA** | ESG Leader |
| **A / BBB / BB** | Average |
| **B / CCC** | ESG Laggard |

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfall"}
The score corresponds to a **relative ranking** within the sector — not an absolute measure of environmental virtue.
:::

- **Trend**: ESG scores increase over time (Lundström 2021) → real improvement + reporting effect

### Carbon Emissions — Scopes

| Scope | Content | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Direct emissions | Boilers, vehicle fleet |
| **2** | Indirect energy consumed | Purchased electricity |
| **3** | All other upstream/downstream emissions | Product use by customers |

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfall"}
Scope 3 is often the largest but the hardest to measure — ignoring it skews the analysis.
:::

### ITR Score (*Implied Temperature Rise*)

- Implied temperature rise if all companies behaved like the one analysed
- **Target**: ≤ 1.5 °C (Paris Agreement)
- High score (3–4 °C) = very concerning

### SDGs (*Sustainable Development Goals*)

17 UN objectives (2015, horizon 2030) — now **quantified** in portfolio analyses

| No. | Objective | No. | Objective |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No poverty | 10 | Reduced inequalities |
| 2 | Zero hunger | 11 | Sustainable cities |
| 3 | Good health & well-being | 12 | Responsible consumption |
| 4 | Quality education | 13 | Climate action |
| 5 | Gender equality | 14 | Life below water |
| 6 | Clean water | 15 | Life on land |
| 7 | Clean energy | 16 | Peace & justice |
| 8 | Decent work | 17 | Partnerships |
| 9 | Industry & innovation | | |

## The 7 ESG Strategies (Eurosif, 2019)

| # | Strategy | Short description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Exclusion** | Exclude sectors / normative / worst-in-class |
| 2 | **Values** (*Norms-based*) | Filter according to international standards (UN, ILO) |
| 3 | **Positive selection** (*Best-in-class*) | Overweight ESG leaders by sector |
| 4 | **Thematic** | Steer towards sustainable themes (e.g. green bonds) |
| 5 | **Integration** | ESG integrated into the entire management process |
| 6 | **Engagement** | Voting at AGMs + dialogue with management |
| 7 | **Impact** | Measurable, intentional and additional impact |

### Key points by strategy

**Exclusion** → simple to implement · does not change the company · possible sector bias

**Best-in-class** → maintains diversification · a company can be "better" while still polluting

**Integration** → ESG = long-term financial risk · ESG benchmarks · dashboards

**Engagement** → resource-intensive · often mutualised (coalitions) · long-term results

**Impact** → 3 conditions: **intentionality** + **measurability** + **additionality**

---

## Practical case: compenswiss (end 2022)

### The 4 axes

| Axis | Concrete actions |
|---|---|
| **1. Integration** | ESG benchmarks · ESG Dashboard · Swiss Climate Scores |
| **2. Voting** | ~100 AGMs/year in Switzerland · external consultant · defined voting rules |
| **3. Engagement** | Via ASIR (co-founded) · 150+ issuers · themes: human rights, labour, environment |
| **4. Exclusions** | ~100 companies · normative + coal (threshold lowered 50 % → 30 %) |

### Carbon footprint analysis (June 2020 – Dec. 2022)

- Unit: **tCO₂e / M$ invested**
- Trajectories: Portfolio > Benchmark > Ideal benchmark
- General trend: **decreasing** for all three curves
- Visible impact of lowering the coal threshold

::: {.callout-note title="Key lesson"}
Without ESG data and tools → no steering possible. **Coverage** (% of assets with ESG data) and **time traversal** are critical operational issues.
:::

### Engagement via ASIR

- Total number of cases: **rising** (driven by human rights)
- Thematic distribution: **stable** (ethics, environment, labour)
- Engagement = **long-term** process

### Voting in Switzerland

- Share "all motions accepted": **rising** (law on abusive remuneration)
- Share "one motion rejected": **stable** (mainly executive remuneration)

## Critical Points / Pitfalls

::: {.callout-warning title="Pitfalls to avoid"}

- **Rater divergence**: an ESG score varies by provider → do not treat a single score as absolute truth

- **Relative ≠ Absolute**: being "best-in-class" in a polluting sector does not mean being virtuous in absolute terms

- **Greenwashing**: a company can communicate on SDGs without real action — validate with third-party data

- **Scope 3 ignored**: often the most important perimeter, but also the hardest to measure

- **Rising scores over time**: may reflect real improvement OR simply better reporting

- **Engagement ≠ immediate result**: the impact of shareholder dialogue is measured over several years

:::

---

## Final Summary

::: {.callout-note title="Essential messages"}

1. Current human activities **are not sustainable**

2. Finance **cannot solve everything** but can steer capital

3. **ESG** = 3 pillars · 10 themes · 37 issues · relative sector-based scoring

4. **Scopes 1/2/3** and **ITR** = tools for measuring climate impact

5. **7 strategies** exist, often combined in practice

6. **ESG data** is central: coverage, quality, temporality

7. Sustainable finance = **young, growing, standardising** field

:::
